# PartyService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("PartyService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Keeps the parties of an online game: players who play together across its worlds, channels and instances. A party is the manager's, so it is known wherever its members are; a world on its own keeps its own.

A member is who the game knows a player by: `Player.AccountId`, or `Player.PublicKey` where the game has no accounts (`MemberIdOf` says which). A party has at most eight members (`[parties] size` in `servers.toml`), a player is in one at a time, and a member who drops and comes back within five minutes is still in it. `NetworkService:TravelGroup` and `InstanceService:CreateInstanceAsync` take a party's id. What else a party means, such as loot or quests, is the game's. Server side only.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Methods

### `AcceptAsync(party: string, invitee: Player): ({ Id: string, Leader: string, Members: {string} }?, string?)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Puts an invited player into the party. Refused with `NotInvited`, `InParty` or `Full`.

### `CreateAsync(leader: Player): ({ Id: string, Leader: string, Members: {string} }?, string?)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Makes a party led by `leader`, and returns it as `{ Id, Leader, Members }`. Returns nil and the reason, `InParty`, where the player is in one already. Each of these methods answers a refusal so, and never raises for one.

### `DeclineAsync(party: string, invitee: Player): ({ Id: string, Leader: string, Members: {string} }?, string?)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Lets an invitation go unanswered no longer.

### `GetPartyAsync(player: Player): { Id: string, Leader: string, Members: {string} }?`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

The party `player` is in, or nil.

### `InviteAsync(party: string, by: Player, invitee: Player | string): ({ Id: string, Leader: string, Members: {string} }?, string?)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Invites `invitee` into the party on behalf of `by`, a member of it: `Invited` fires in the invitee's world. `invitee` is a player in this world, or a member id (`MemberIdOf`) for one in another. Refused with `NoParty`, `NotMember`, `InParty` or `Full`.

### `KickAsync(party: string, member: string): ({ Id: string, Leader: string, Members: {string} }?, string?)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Takes a member out of the party, online or not, by `MemberIdOf`. Who may kick whom is the game's to decide before it calls this.

### `LeaveAsync(member: Player): ({ Id: string, Leader: string, Members: {string} }?, string?)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Takes a player out of their party. A leader who leaves hands it to the member who joined first after them, and the last one leaving ends it, when it returns nil and no reason.

### `MemberIdOf(player: Player): string`

Who `player` is in a party: their `AccountId`, or their `PublicKey` where they have none.

### `SetLeaderAsync(party: string, member: string): ({ Id: string, Leader: string, Members: {string} }?, string?)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Makes a member, by `MemberIdOf`, the party's leader.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Changed(party: string)`

Fires in every world one of the party's members is in when it changes: a member joins or leaves, or the leader changes. Also when it ends; `GetPartyAsync` then finds none.

### `Invited(player: Player, party: string, by: string)`

Fires in the world of a player invited into a party, with who invited them, by `MemberIdOf`. What the player is shown, and how they answer, is the game's.
